items.name: Elks Most Valuable Student
items.summary: 500 four-year awards for seniors, judged on scholarship, leadership and financial need. U.S. citizens only; no Elks connection needed.

items.name: Jack Kent Cooke College Scholarship
items.summary: Last-dollar funding for high-achieving seniors with financial need, renewable through a bachelor's degree.

items.name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
items.summary: For Black/African American seniors showing academic excellence, leadership, community service and financial need.

items.name: Live Más Scholarship
items.summary: Passion-based: apply with a short video about what drives you instead of grades or test scores.

items.name: Voice of Democracy
items.summary: Audio-essay contest on a patriotic theme, entered through a local VFW Post. Local and state prizes too.

items.name: Coolidge Scholarship
items.summary: Full four-year merit scholarship for juniors with an interest in public policy, economics or the humanities.

items.name: Burger King Scholars
items.summary: Weighs GPA, work experience, activities, community service and need. Closes early once it hits its application cap.

items.name: Dell Scholars Program
items.summary: For Pell-eligible seniors in a college-readiness program, with a laptop, textbook credits and coaching through college.

items.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
items.summary: For students 18 or under who completed a significant project in STEM, literature, music or philosophy. 2027 application opens Nov 2.

items.name: HSF Scholar Program
items.summary: For students of Hispanic heritage with a 3.0+ GPA. Opens in January; needs a completed FAFSA.

items.name: Coca-Cola Scholars
items.summary: 150 seniors chosen for leadership and service impact. Opens each August; plan for next year if you're a junior.

items.name: The Gates Scholarship
items.summary: Last-dollar full scholarship for Pell-eligible minority seniors with strong academics and leadership.

items.name: QuestBridge National College Match
items.summary: Matches high-achieving, low-income seniors with full scholarships at partner colleges. Juniors can apply to the College Prep Scholars program in spring.

items.name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
items.summary: For seniors who have overcome significant adversity and show financial need and community involvement.

items.name: National Merit Scholarship
items.summary: You enter by taking the PSAT/NMSQT in October of junior year. Top scorers become Semifinalists the next fall.

items.name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
items.summary: The top research competition for seniors: submit an original science, math or engineering research project.

items.name: NCWIT Award for Aspirations in Computing
items.summary: Honors women, genderqueer and nonbinary students for computing achievements and interests. National and regional affiliate awards.

items.name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
items.summary: The longest-running recognition program for teen artists and writers. Regional deadlines are usually December–January.

items.name: YoungArts National Arts Competition
items.summary: For artists 15–18 in visual, literary, design and performing arts. Winners get cash awards and mentorship.

items.name: United States Senate Youth Program
items.summary: Two delegates per state, chosen from students in elected student-government or civic positions. Selection runs through the state.

items.name: Cal Grant (via FAFSA or CADAA)
items.amountText: Covers UC/CSU tuition or helps at private colleges
items.summary: California's state grant. You apply by filing the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application and a verified GPA by the state deadline.

items.name: Congressional Award
items.summary: Earn bronze to gold medals for goals in volunteer service, personal development, fitness and exploration. Your comp hours count.

items.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
items.org: Center for Excellence in Education at MIT
items.summary: Six-week summer research program at MIT for juniors. Free to students and highly selective.

items.name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
items.summary: Free six-week college-level seminar in critical Black studies or anti-oppressive studies for sophomores and juniors.

items.name: COSMOS
items.summary: Four-week residential STEM program at UC Irvine, Davis, San Diego or Santa Cruz for California students. Financial aid available.

items.name: MITES Summer
items.summary: Free six-week residential STEM program at MIT for rising seniors, especially those underrepresented in STEM.

items.name: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
items.summary: Advanced summer math program covering abstract algebra, number theory and research-style problem solving.

items.name: Ross Mathematical Program
items.summary: Six-week number theory program built around deep problem sets. Known for teaching students to think like mathematicians.

items.name: PROMYS
items.summary: Six-week summer program in number theory with an application problem set.

items.name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
items.summary: Five-week summer program where students choose their own advanced math classes. Entry is by a qualifying quiz.

items.name: UCSB Research Mentorship Program
items.summary: Six-week program pairing students with UCSB mentors on an interdisciplinary research project.

items.name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
items.summary: Free online programming contests held through the winter. Climb from Bronze to Platinum.

items.name: AMC 10/12
items.summary: The first round of the U.S. math olympiad pipeline, taken in November through your school or a host site.

items.name: Congressional App Challenge
items.summary: Build an app and submit it to your representative's district competition. Winners are shown in the Capitol. (comp. is an entry!)

items.name: Hack Club
items.summary: Nonprofit network of teen coders: start a club, join hackathons and "you ship, we ship" programs that fund your projects.

items.name: HOBY Leadership Seminar
items.summary: Weekend leadership seminar for sophomores, usually through a school nomination. Ask your counselor in the fall.

items.name: Boys State / Girls State
items.summary: A week building a mock state government, for juniors. Students are nominated through their school, usually in spring.
